L'oeuvre de Zakia Safa Zakir Hussein, ta: The work of Zakia Safa Zakir Hussein, a henna tattoo artist.
C’est par hasard que l’on rencontre Zaki: We meet Zakia Safa Zakir Hussein by chance, on a Wednesday evening in April, at the Khadija Mosque, where she has been involved since her teens. The 18-year-old student devotes her free time to giving back to the community, especially during the month of Ramadan.
Avec une de ses collègues, Zakia Safa a: Together with one of her colleagues, Zakia Safa decided to put her skills as a henna tattoo artist to good use. Usually done on the hands and feet, this temporary tattoo is an ancestral practice that is common at family celebrations and Muslim religious ceremonies, whether for aesthetic or religious reasons.
Chaque mercredi à partir de 14 h, les je: Every Wednesday starting at 2 p.m., the young tattoo artists offer their services at the Khadija Mosque. They charge $10 per hand. “All the money raised will go toward building a mosque in Punjab, India,” Zakia explains. Beyond her generosity, Zakia is an entrepreneur in the making. She has launched a henna business that takes her all over the island of Montréal. To gain the resources she needs to grow her business, she decided to pursue studies in entrepreneurship at Dawson College. “I started my business on Instagram.
Au début, j’y publiais des photos, mais: At first, I posted photos there, but I didn’t have many clients. So I kind of gave up on it,” says the artist. Today, Zakia has more than 1,000 followers on her Instagram page, and she is receiving more and more messages from people who would like to book her services. “A lot of people have contacted me to make appointments, and my business keeps growing,” she says happily.
C’est pour soutenir sa famille que la je: The young woman first went into business to support her family. “Ever since I was little, my parents have given me the best life possible. I went to private schools, which are very expensive. My parents had to shell out nearly $5,000 a year to send me there,” she says.
Aujourd’hui, Zakia Safa souhaite rendre: Today, Zakia Safa wants to return the favour to her parents and, in turn, contribute to her family’s well-being. “I’m trying to give back to my parents by making as much money as I can and hoping to give them everything they were able to give me.”
